**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prevent pending-notice recovery from requesting a stopped PR review**

If Linear rejects `avisarComprobaciones` and the maintainer adds `babysitter:stop` before the next tick, `driver.ts`'s `finishStopping()` invokes the pending graph to deliver that notice. This new edge then proceeds directly to `pedirRevision`, publishing `@codex review` even though the driver has already observed the stop label. Previously, recovery only finished the pending notification before stopping; it now starts a new external action and consumes a review against the maintainer's stop request. Preserve delivery of the pending notice, but prevent recovery from entering the review-request node once the PR is stopped.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate the current push before recovering a review request**

If Linear rejects the checks-finished notice for push A and push B arrives before recovery, `driver.ts` observes B but resumes the pending graph with `graph.invoke(null, config)`, retaining A's snapshot. After delivering the notice, this node publishes a request marked for A, although `@codex review` reviews the current head B—even if B's checks are pending or failing. The same problem occurs when recovering a failed request. Unlike a push racing with publication, the changed head is already known to the driver here. Preserve pending-notice delivery, but revalidate the current head and its checks before allowing recovery to publish a review request.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Real, arreglado en f55e8d2: al reintentar un nodo pendiente, si el driver ya ve otro SHA, termina el aviso pero se salta `pedirRevision` (`updateState` como ese nodo) y deja el hilo a la espera del revisor; la foto siguiente lo lleva al push nuevo, que pide la suya al pasar sus comprobaciones. Con el mismo SHA se reintenta como antes. Tres tests en `driver.test.ts`; `design.md` (decisión 6) y README en 38f0872.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Route failed checks directly to the final notification**

When all checks finish with at least one failure and there is no review of the current push, this branch still returns `checksFinished`, sending the graph through `avisarComprobaciones` into `esperarRevisor`. Since `needsReviewRequest` now deliberately prevents requesting a review for failed checks, the PR waits until the timeout for a review that was never requested, then incorrectly reports an unfinished review alongside the check failure. This contradicts the changed failure scenario in `openspec/changes/pr-review-request/specs/pr-tracking/spec.md`: notify the final failure without waiting for review or publishing the checks-finished notice. Route failed checks directly to the final notification and omit the unfinished-review reason when no review was needed.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Real, pero es el alcance de la otra tarea de la historia, MOO-91 (sección 2 de `openspec/changes/pr-review-request/tasks.md`, pasos 2.1-2.4): `afterChecksWait` distingue pasan y fallan, la arista de comprobaciones fallidas va directa a `avisarEstadoFinal` y el estado final sin `reviewSince` no dice que la revisión no ha terminado. El change la planifica como una PR aparte, detrás de esta, y no se mezclan dos tareas en una PR. Hasta entonces no empeora nada respecto a `main`: con una comprobación fallida, la PR ya esperaba una revisión que la *Automatic review* no lanza en los push siguientes y acababa a los 30 min desde el push; sin `reviewSince`, el reloj sigue contando desde el push.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_
